families.name: Washing machine
families.primary_function: Clean, rinse and extract water from declared laundry loads while remaining safe and serviceable.
critical_constraints: Water containment and leakage prevention under static and dynamic load
Guarding, interlock, electrical isolation, thermal and heavy-rotating assembly hazards
Tub/bearing fatigue, vibration, noise and tolerance retention over declared life
families.service_boundary: U0 for intended filter/dispenser/cleaning tasks; qualified work for internal mains, heater, drive, tub and heavy rotating assemblies.

variants.description: Frozen retail washer baseline with exact model/revision and documented functional state.
variants.hypothesis: Provides control function, repair task time, parts supply and resource use.
tradeoffs: May contain non-serviceable tub or integrated modules.
Used donor condition can confound function and failure-history comparisons.
required_tests: Frozen task-by-task disassembly and repair protocol.
Matched successful-load energy/water/function pilot.

variants.description: Reversible access path to documented high-value wear/repair points and diagnostic references.
variants.hypothesis: Reduces total restoration burden without making the structure, seals or connectors less reliable.
tradeoffs: Access panels and extra connectors add cost and tolerance stacks.
Service access can compromise stiffness, noise or water containment.
required_tests: Timed fault-to-restoration and assembly-error tests.
Leak, guarded spin, vibration and durability checks.

variants.description: Separately serviceable bearing/seal boundary compared with a sealed tub assembly.
variants.hypothesis: May reduce discarded assembly mass and bearing repair cost if sealing, alignment and fatigue remain acceptable.
tradeoffs: Bolted joints can leak or loosen; precision and reassembly effort increase.
Benefits depend on bearing incidence, parts supply and labour cost.
required_tests: Seal/vibration/fatigue test with tolerance records.
Full lifecycle break-even model including repeated repair and rework.

families.name: Dishwasher
families.primary_function: Clean and dry declared loads of crockery while managing spray, drainage, heat and leakage.
critical_constraints: Water leakage, overfill and flood containment
Heater/electrical and hot-water exposure boundaries
Wash coverage, drying outcome, hygiene and correct filter/spray performance
families.service_boundary: User access only for manual-authorized filters, racks and spray-arm tasks; internal sump, pump, heater and live electrical work require qualified procedures.

variants.description: Frozen retail dishwasher with documented eco/programme function and known condition.
variants.hypothesis: Establishes cleaning, drying, leakage, water/energy and service baselines.
tradeoffs: Built-in installation can bias access time.
Programme and loading variation can dominate comparisons.
required_tests: Matched load soils and loading pattern.
Documented toe-kick and wet-path teardown.

variants.description: Front-access wet-service region for filter, sump and selected drain components, with explicit leak containment.
variants.hypothesis: Can make common wet-path faults repairable without removing unrelated electronics or the whole tank.
tradeoffs: More service boundaries can add gasket and leak failure modes.
Service region can increase price and packaging volume.
required_tests: Leak testing after repeated service cycles.
Cleaning/drying non-inferiority and restore-time study.

variants.description: Separate wet-process module and electronics/actuation plane with clear wiring and water-path separation.
variants.hypothesis: Reduces collateral teardown and keeps wet failures from forcing electronics replacement.
tradeoffs: Longer hoses/connectors and wiring can increase parts and assembly error.
Wet/electrical segregation may complicate compactness.
required_tests: Water path and ingress tests after repair.
Harness reassembly/error and fault-isolation trials.

families.name: Refrigerator/freezer
families.primary_function: Maintain safe, stable chilled/frozen storage across declared ambient and loading conditions.
critical_constraints: Sealed refrigerant and pressure boundaries; flammable refrigerant-specific precautions where applicable
Insulation, door sealing, condensation and cabinet thermal bridges
Temperature stability and food-storage functional limits
families.service_boundary: Intended gasket and accessible air-side maintenance separated from qualified electrical/refrigerant service; never equate a service module with permission to open a sealed circuit.

variants.description: Frozen retail refrigerator/freezer baseline with model, refrigerant identity and temperature performance recorded.
variants.hypothesis: Sets stable temperature, energy and service baseline over declared ambient/load.
tradeoffs: Ambient climate and door-opening patterns strongly affect measurements.
Cabinet/insulation lifetime differs from control electronics lifetime.
required_tests: Temperature mapping and energy test at declared conditions.
Seal/hinge/defrost/fan access task trial.

variants.description: Accessible fan, air path, defrost drain and sensor/control service points with a sealed thermal boundary.
variants.hypothesis: Routine air-side faults can be resolved without touching the refrigerant circuit.
tradeoffs: Added panels and ducts can introduce thermal leaks/noise/condensate.
Fan/coil arrangement varies across topologies.
required_tests: Airflow and temperature uniformity before/after service.
Condensate, dust, gasket and energy tests.

variants.description: Qualified-service replaceable sealed refrigeration subsystem as a design concept, retaining product-specific refrigerant procedures.
variants.hypothesis: Could isolate expensive thermal work from a durable cabinet when lifecycle costs support exchange.
tradeoffs: Factory joints or service connections can add leak risk and losses.
Module inventory, refrigerant, charge and certification burden can overwhelm benefits.
required_tests: Qualified leak/pressure/reliability and applicable conformity tests.
Full lifecycle comparison including evacuation/recovery and recommissioning.

families.name: Heat-pump tumble dryer
families.primary_function: Remove water from declared laundry loads efficiently while meeting final-moisture and textile-care requirements.
critical_constraints: Sealed refrigerant circuit and qualified pressure/thermal/electrical service
Airflow, lint accumulation, accessible filter and cleanable heat-exchanger paths
Condensate drainage, humidity/temperature sensing and fire prevention
families.service_boundary: U0 filter and manual-authorized accessible cleaning; refrigerant, power electronics, heater and guarded drive tasks remain qualified service.

variants.description: Frozen retail heat-pump dryer with energy, load, initial moisture and final moisture recorded.
variants.hypothesis: Provides baseline drying energy, cycle time and maintenance burden.
tradeoffs: Inlet moisture varies with washer spin performance.
Fouling state and ambient humidity influence comparison.
required_tests: Matched load and initial-moisture protocol.
Lint/condensate maintenance disassembly study.

variants.description: Owner-accessible lint/airflow/condensate service path and replaceable air-side fan/filter submodules.
variants.hypothesis: Can prevent routine cleaning from requiring deep cabinet disassembly and sustain airflow.
tradeoffs: More access seals may leak bypass air or noise.
Serviceable heat exchanger geometry may be harder to optimize.
required_tests: Repeated fouling/cleaning and pressure-drop tests.
Drying efficiency and post-service moisture distribution.

variants.description: Distinct qualified thermal service boundary for heat-pump subsystem and separated low-voltage diagnostic/sensor plane.
variants.hypothesis: Could reduce collateral replacements while leaving refrigerant work within qualified service.
tradeoffs: Extra thermal and electrical interfaces can lose efficiency or add failure modes.
Module exchange cost can remain high due to evacuation/recommissioning requirements.
required_tests: Qualified leak/energy/durability verification.
Restoration cost and parts delivery sensitivity.

families.name: Washer-dryer combo
families.primary_function: Provide wash and dry services in one installation while meeting both output specifications within acceptable time and resource use.
critical_constraints: Combined cycle time and loss of the whole appliance from a single-point failure
Wet, airflow, condensate and thermal/refrigerant interactions
Both wash quality and dry final-moisture limits
useful_output_metrics: kWh and water per complete cycle
families.service_boundary: Washer wet-service and dryer air/thermal boundary remain independently diagnosable where feasible; qualified hazardous components cannot be downgraded because the device is integrated.

variants.description: Existing combo baseline with complete wash and dry cycle recorded.
variants.hypothesis: Establishes a matched baseline for convenience, throughput, maintenance and whole-cycle resource use.
tradeoffs: Integrated architecture can cause a fault in one function to disable both.
Cycle times and thermal transitions complicate comparisons.
required_tests: Full combined-cycle measurement and fault mapping.
Functional comparison to separate washer+dryer context.

variants.description: Separately mapped and accessible wash hydraulic, air/condensate, and control subsystems.
variants.hypothesis: May prevent a localized function failure from forcing replacement of a shared assembly.
tradeoffs: More interfaces can increase assembly effort and leak/fault coupling.
Packaging may constrain access and thermal performance.
required_tests: Fault isolation and post-repair wash/dry verification.
Access and cycle performance under equal loads.

variants.description: Shared service/evidence contract plus moisture-aware wash extraction and drying control; no presumed shared physical heat pump.
variants.hypothesis: Could lower whole-laundry energy/elapsed time through better initial moisture and service coordination.
tradeoffs: Sensors and control logic add calibration and failure modes.
Benefits may depend on load mix, spin limits and textiles.
required_tests: Matched successful wash+dry outcomes and whole-cycle energy.
Sensor fault, safe abstention and cross-function recovery tests.

families.name: Heat-pump water heater
families.primary_function: Deliver declared hot-water volume and temperature with acceptable recovery, standing losses and safe pressure/thermal behaviour.
critical_constraints: Tank/pressure/temperature safety and potable-water compatibility
Condensate, corrosion/anode, air filters/fan and thermal-system access
Refrigerant and high-current parts remain qualified service
families.service_boundary: User-level checks limited to documented external maintenance; tank, pressure, heater, electrical and sealed refrigerant work require product-specific qualified service.

variants.description: Baseline tank heat-pump unit with inlet conditions, ambient, hot-water draw profile and recovery measured.
variants.hypothesis: Sets delivered service and maintenance baseline under declared usage.
tradeoffs: Hot-water draw profiles strongly affect measured efficiency.
Installation and incoming water conditions change results.
required_tests: Declared draw/recovery and standby-loss protocol.
Service access, condensate and corrosion/anode plan review.

variants.description: Long-life insulated tank/hydronic section with independently accessible air-side fan/filter/condensate and replaceable sensors/controls.
variants.hypothesis: Can isolate air-side and control faults from the durable tank while supporting safe service.
tradeoffs: More connections create leak and corrosion interfaces.
Air-side modules and tank form factor may increase footprint.
required_tests: Leak/pressure and thermal safety tests.
Delivered hot-water, recovery and servicing trials.

variants.description: Qualified heat-pump module plus optional PV/thermal-storage scheduling layer with local standalone operating mode.
variants.hypothesis: May shift thermal load when energy is cheaper/available without sacrificing hot-water service.
tradeoffs: Extra valves, tanks and controller increase cost and failure modes.
Savings depend on local climate, tariff, PV and draw profile.
required_tests: Matched draw profile, standby loss and lifecycle sensitivity.
Offline/no-network safe operation and fault-injection tests.

families.name: Residential HVAC / air-source heat pump
families.primary_function: Deliver heating/cooling and indoor comfort across declared outdoor climate, building load and part-load operation.
critical_constraints: Refrigerant pressure and product-specific service qualification
Airflow/coil/condensate/frost management and electrical protection
Seasonal performance, comfort, humidity, acoustics and defrost behaviour
families.service_boundary: Filters and specified accessible air-side checks separated from qualified refrigerant, high-voltage and pressure work; indoor/outdoor compatibility is model-specific.

variants.description: Baseline installed heat-pump system with declared indoor/outdoor pairing, climate and load profile.
variants.hypothesis: Sets seasonal function, noise, comfort, energy and service baseline.
tradeoffs: Installation quality and load sizing dominate results.
Seasonal metrics require appropriate weather/load bins.
required_tests: Declared climate/load and seasonal test profile.
Service access and diagnostic task review.

variants.description: Distinct air-handler service region for filters, fan, drain and sensors, separate from qualified thermal circuit work.
variants.hypothesis: Can lower routine maintenance time while protecting refrigerant and electrical boundaries.
tradeoffs: Extra panels and connectors can increase airflow leaks/noise.
Outdoor coil exposure and corrosion remain location-specific.
required_tests: Airflow/pressure, condensate and acoustic checks.
Seasonal output and safe post-service verification.

variants.description: Versioned control/evidence contracts with optional thermal-storage/PV load scheduling and independent safety control.
variants.hypothesis: May improve load shifting without making basic heating/cooling dependent on cloud services.
tradeoffs: More valves/storage/control add maintenance points.
Savings depend on building, tariff, climate and user preferences.
required_tests: Part-load/defrost/comfort profile with and without orchestration.
Network-loss, sensor failure and safe operating-state tests.

families.name: Oven, cooker and hob
families.primary_function: Deliver controlled cooking/heat output and temperature uniformity with reliable thermal, fire and electrical/gas protection.
critical_constraints: Hot-surface, fire, high-power electrical and gas-specific hazards where applicable
Thermal insulation, cavity/seal integrity and temperature calibration
Distinct technology branches: resistance, induction and gas are not physically interchangeable
families.service_boundary: Owner scope limited to documented cleaning and accessible parts; internal heating/power/gas/insulation work is qualified service.

variants.description: Baseline oven/hob with selected technology and declared cooking task/temperature programme.
variants.hypothesis: Establishes cooking outcome, energy, access and service baseline.
tradeoffs: Food/task and vessel choices affect results.
Different heat technologies require separate test plans.
required_tests: Temperature mapping and matched cooking tasks.
Door/seal/control disassembly and protection review.

variants.description: Separately replaceable zone-level component/control/heater interfaces where technically justified.
variants.hypothesis: Can avoid discarding a whole hob/cavity for a localized failure.
tradeoffs: Zone modules may increase wiring/connectors and thermal interaction.
Induction and gas technology need separate validated architectures.
required_tests: Temperature uniformity and protection after replacement.
Repeat assembly, insulation, fire/thermal cycling tests.

variants.description: Serviceable door/seal/hinge, controls and cooling-airflow modules around a durable insulated structure.
variants.hypothesis: May extend structural service life while replacing likely wear/control components separately.
tradeoffs: Service seams can harm insulation, cooling airflow or hot-surface performance.
Thermal cycles can loosen fasteners and deform interfaces.
required_tests: Thermal-cycle, seal, surface-temperature and electrical tests.
Repair time and energy under matched cooking output.

families.name: Residential ventilation / heat-recovery ventilator
families.primary_function: Deliver declared fresh-air flow and heat recovery while managing filtration, noise, condensation and cross-contamination.
critical_constraints: Air hygiene and separation of supply/exhaust streams
Condensate/frost control, sealing and core/bypass operation
Airflow, pressure drop, acoustic and electrical safety
families.service_boundary: User filter maintenance only as documented; fan electrical and core/bypass balancing tasks follow product-specific qualified procedures.

variants.description: Baseline ventilation/HRV unit with installation and duct configuration frozen.
variants.hypothesis: Sets airflow, recovery, pressure, noise and filter service baseline.
tradeoffs: Duct design and installation dominate performance.
Weather, frost and fouling impact measurement.
required_tests: Airflow/pressure and heat recovery measurement.
Filter/core access and condensate inspection trial.

variants.description: Accessible filter, fan and replaceable heat-recovery core with independent seals and clear flow orientation.
variants.hypothesis: Allows maintenance or core replacement without removing unrelated duct runs.
tradeoffs: Cassette seals may leak or bypass; extra interfaces increase pressure drop.
Core access can affect acoustic and thermal insulation.
required_tests: Leak/bypass and heat-recovery tests after service cycles.
Filter pressure, fan power, sound and rebalancing burden.

variants.description: Reuse airflow service conventions and evidence contracts with HVAC while retaining ventilation-specific flow and frost controls.
variants.hypothesis: May reduce technician training and improve documentation without imposing universal fan/core hardware.
tradeoffs: Common conventions may conceal product-specific pressure/acoustic requirements.
Frost, humidity and indoor-air quality are site-dependent.
required_tests: Cross-family usability/assembly study.
Product-specific flow, condensation, frost and cross-contamination validation.

design_patterns.name: Service spine
design_patterns.mechanism: Deliberate reversible access paths and component identification for declared common repair tasks.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce total restore effort and reassembly uncertainty on high-value repair paths.
failure_modes: Access cut-outs can reduce stiffness or worsen sealing.
Extra panels/fasteners can increase cost or loosen under cycling.

design_patterns.name: Smallest justified repair unit
design_patterns.mechanism: Compare component, functional submodule and major assembly replacement for each fault class.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Minimize lifecycle burden without creating uneconomic micro-repair or oversized modules.
failure_modes: Small modules may be uneconomic or impossible to calibrate safely.
Large modules discard functional material and increase part cost.
validation_metrics: all-in restore cost per fault class
discarded material mass per verified repair

design_patterns.name: Hazard islands
design_patterns.mechanism: Separate user task boundaries, qualified internal work and sealed/high-energy systems into explicit service tiers.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Improve safe access while preserving product-specific hazard controls.
failure_modes: Misleading visual boundary can invite unsafe opening.
Interfaces can compromise insulation, containment or qualification.
validation_metrics: critical safety findings and post-repair verification completeness

design_patterns.name: Separated wet/air/thermal/control paths
design_patterns.mechanism: Make fluid, airflow/condensate, thermal and control routes visible and separately serviceable where justified.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Prevent one subsystem fault from forcing unrelated subsystem disassembly or replacement.
failure_modes: Longer interfaces can leak, foul or increase pressure/thermal losses.
Segregation may increase packaging and assembly cost.

design_patterns.name: Diagnostics before replacement
design_patterns.mechanism: Versioned diagnostic graphs with competing hypotheses, safe discriminating checks, unknown states and receipts.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce unnecessary component swaps, false confident diagnoses and repeat visits.
failure_modes: Sensor drift or stale/contradictory telemetry may mislead diagnosis.
Proprietary access or cloud dependence can block repair.

design_patterns.name: Successful-output control
design_patterns.mechanism: Use measured useful service outputs, not cycle commands or nominal settings, to evaluate resource use.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Avoid apparent efficiency gains that degrade cleaning, drying, cooling, cooking or comfort.
failure_modes: Poor reference loads/tasks make comparisons incomparable.
Sensor/calibration errors hide degraded output.

design_patterns.name: Durable shell + replaceable wear layer
design_patterns.mechanism: Keep durable shells/insulation/structures separate from justified wear, seal, sensor and control replacements.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Extend useful structural life when replaceable wear parts actually drive repair or retirement.
failure_modes: Service seams can weaken a pressure/thermal envelope.
Shell durability may not economically outlast other core components.

design_patterns.name: Repair-resilient parts identity
design_patterns.mechanism: Exact model/revision part-fit records, supersession, source independence, delivery and returns.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce parts misorders and long outages without treating catalogue visibility as proof of fit.
failure_modes: Multiple sellers can rely on one upstream supplier.
Supersession can break physical/electrical/firmware compatibility.
validation_metrics: P50/P90 delivered lead time and misorder rate

design_patterns.name: Selective disassembly and recovery
design_patterns.mechanism: Use reversible joints and material labels where a realistic repair/refurbishment/recovery path exists.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce collateral breakage and improve reuse/material recovery at service/end-of-life.
failure_modes: Reversible joints can compromise sealing/retention or add material.
Mixed-material bonding may still be best for durability/safety in some places.

design_patterns.name: Shared service contracts, specialized hardware
design_patterns.mechanism: Reuse diagnostics, identity, safe-state, part-fit and post-repair schemas; keep physical components product-specific until qualified.
design_patterns.benefit_hypothesis: Reuse learning and training without unsafe universal-component assumptions.
failure_modes: Overgeneric schemas may omit unique hazards or useful-output metrics.
A shared controller/protocol can introduce correlated failure or cyber exposure.
validation_metrics: independent service task success and correlated-failure analysis

hybrid_candidates.name: Cross-family service contract platform
hybrid_candidates.combination: Use stable identity, diagnostic evidence, safe-state, part-fit, role-boundary and post-repair receipt contracts across different appliances.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Transfer service knowledge and auditability between appliance families without falsely standardizing pumps, compressors or boards.
non_claims: No physical component interchangeability is claimed.
No safety authority is assigned to the diagnostic/control platform.
key_trades: Shared schema must preserve unique thermal, fluid, electrical and mechanical hazards.
Common platform failure or cyber exposure could correlate across products.
discriminating_tests: Mutate one family's hazard/unknown fields and prove the auditor fails closed.
Conduct held-out cross-family service-task data mapping with product experts.

hybrid_candidates.name: Washer/dishwasher wet-service conventions
hybrid_candidates.combination: Reuse service access, leak containment evidence, part identity and wet-path diagnostic conventions while retaining product-specific pumps, hoses, pressures and materials.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce service learning and access burden on water-handling repair tasks.
non_claims: No shared pump, seal, hose or wetted component is claimed interchangeable.
No common pressure/temperature rating is assumed.
key_trades: Detergents, thermal cycles, hydraulics and sanitary constraints differ.
More service boundaries can add leak points.
discriminating_tests: Cross-family task usability and service-documentation study.
Product-specific leak, cleaning performance and connector endurance tests.

hybrid_candidates.name: Air-side service cassette family
hybrid_candidates.combination: Reuse access, filter/fan/condensate inspection conventions and module identity for the air-side while preserving product-specific coil/fan/pressure performance.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Make routine airflow maintenance easier and decouple it from sealed thermal-service procedures.
non_claims: No fan, filter, coil or airflow cassette is claimed universally interchangeable.
No refrigerant access is granted by air-side modularization.
key_trades: Pressure drop, noise, moisture, dust and airflow geometries differ.
Air bypass/seal failure can degrade efficiency and hygiene.
discriminating_tests: Measure pressure drop, flow, sound, condensate and post-service output for each family.
Timed clean/service trials with controlled fouling and repeat assembly.

hybrid_candidates.name: Qualified thermal-service boundary
hybrid_candidates.combination: Use common documentation and diagnosis semantics to distinguish product-specific sealed thermal subsystems from outer airflow/water service; refrigerant-side work stays qualified.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce collateral replacement and make service scope more predictable for thermal products.
non_claims: No refrigerant connector, charge, compressor, coil or thermal module compatibility is claimed.
No consumer refrigerant handling is proposed.
key_trades: Joints and module swaps may increase leak, efficiency and commissioning costs.
Refrigerant flammability/pressure/safety qualifications differ by product.
discriminating_tests: Product-specific leak and pressure qualification by competent lab.
Compare qualified restore cost, recommissioning effort, leak incidence and lifecycle energy.

hybrid_candidates.name: Durable shell plus replaceable wear layer
hybrid_candidates.combination: Separate longer-lived tub support, cabinet/insulation or cavity from justified wear items such as bearings/seals/gaskets/hinges where design allows.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Extend structural life and reduce assembly-level disposal when a wear part can be changed without degrading the safety/function envelope.
non_claims: No universal seal/bearing/hinge geometry or fit is claimed.
A bolted/reversible joint is not assumed superior to a welded/bonded joint.
key_trades: Sealing, fatigue, thermal cycling, corrosion and tolerances may worsen.
Labour and spare-part availability can outweigh material savings.
discriminating_tests: Physical disassembly and full reassembly test with measured damage and time.
Seal/fatigue/thermal-vibration tests and lifecycle break-even analysis.

hybrid_candidates.name: Shared evidence contracts with device-specific controllers
hybrid_candidates.combination: Share diagnostic semantics, signed configuration identity, safe-state status and repair receipts, but retain product-specific sensor interfaces and independent protection/control paths.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Lower engineering/support duplication without forcing all products into one fragile control board or cloud dependency.
non_claims: No universal controller board or firmware image is proposed.
Safety protections remain product-specific and cannot be bypassed by the shared service layer.
key_trades: Protocol abstraction can hide stale/contradictory measurements.
Shared dependency can create correlated bugs or cyber risk.
discriminating_tests: Negative/unknown/stale sensor mutation corpus per family.
Offline, network-loss, configuration drift and safety independence tests.

hybrid_candidates.name: Laundry water-removal coordination
hybrid_candidates.combination: Coordinate validated washer extraction/moisture measurements with dryer initial moisture and successful-dry endpoint using explicit interface data.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Reduce drying energy/time for some loads through better initial-state knowledge, while preserving textile and final-moisture requirements.
non_claims: No common physical heat pump or motor is claimed.
No energy reduction is claimed before matched whole-load measurements.
key_trades: Sensing/calibration and compatibility add complexity.
High spin may affect fabrics, noise, residual imbalance or user preferences.
discriminating_tests: Matched laundry cohorts with initial/final moisture, energy and elapsed-time records.
Sensor-loss fallback and cross-device interoperability tests.

hybrid_candidates.name: Thermal resource orchestration
hybrid_candidates.combination: Optional local controller coordinates water-heating, HVAC and any validated PV/thermal storage using tariff/load forecasts while each appliance remains fully functional standalone.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Shift flexible thermal loads where climate, tariffs and installed system make net lifecycle savings possible.
non_claims: No savings or grid service is claimed for an uncharacterized site.
No cloud dependency or network-loss hazard is accepted.
key_trades: Storage/valves/sensors/control add capital cost and failure modes.
PV/tariff/climate/demand vary and may make coordination uneconomic.
discriminating_tests: Site-specific load/tariff simulation followed by metered field trial.
Network loss, bad forecasts, comfort/hot-water reserve and safe fallback tests.

hybrid_candidates.name: Zone-level cooking repair architecture
hybrid_candidates.combination: Keep replaceable zone/heater/power/door/control boundaries around a durable insulated structure, with separate branches for induction, resistance and gas.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Avoid whole-appliance replacement where one independently repairable zone/control/wear interface fails.
non_claims: Induction, resistance and gas components are not interchangeable by default.
No internal user repair of high power, hot cavity or gas train.
key_trades: Thermal/fire/electrical/gas safety and calibration constrain module splits.
More connections may degrade thermal uniformity or repeatability.
discriminating_tests: Per-technology temperature/output and protection checks after service.
Thermal-cycle endurance, electrical/gas qualification and restore-cost comparison.

hybrid_candidates.name: Ventilation/HVAC airflow service conventions
hybrid_candidates.combination: Share service documentation, access design principles and measured airflow/pressure/condensate receipts while retaining each product's flow/core/fan/thermal design.
hybrid_candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Improve maintainer training and routine cleaning without sacrificing ventilation balancing, refrigeration temperature or dryer efficiency.
non_claims: No common airflow component or heat-recovery core is claimed.
No environmental/indoor-air quality superiority is claimed without measurements.
key_trades: Acoustics, static pressure, condensation, lint/dust and hygiene differ.
Common interfaces can add restrictions or leakage.
discriminating_tests: Per-product airflow/pressure/noise/condensate and core function tests.
Controlled fouling, cleaning, leakage and recalibration trials.
